headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: unstructured reads/writes documents while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating a plausible default path for sensitive document content to flow outward and be acted on without…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem or message-queue surface, while B can read/write documents and process text/images. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the main pathway is manual handoff or shared files. That makes hijack plausible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to document-level content.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-generated document text into A as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF A is connected to a shared workspace or clipboard with B, attacker-controlled document content can bridge the pair.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw document text into A.
Add a manual review step before A consumes B output.
Use file naming conventions that distinguish data from instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to B outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read files and has allowlisted network egress; A also has allowlisted egress. If sensitive documents enter B, its outputs can be forwarded or summarized by A, creating a plausible default leakage path. No shared workspace is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced, but the pairwise risk exists.
conditions: IF B processes sensitive documents and A receives B outputs, those contents can leave the local boundary.
IF either agent is pointed at regulated documents, leakage risk increases through allowlisted egress.
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive documents.
Block network egress for A during document handling.
Review B outputs before any external transmission.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on B inputs and A outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, and subprocess capabilities; A has allowlisted network egress. They do not share explicit locking or a common mutable resource in the profiles, but if orchestrated over the same workspace, B can overwrite artifacts that A later exports. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite files A later transmits.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent B instances can race on shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Use read-only mounts for A.
Check file timestamps before export.
requires-engineering: add workspace locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a document-processing agent that can transform inputs into extracted text, and A can then transmit or reuse that output via allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show verification gates, so B's extracted content may be treated as authoritative downstream. This is a default-path inference, not directly observed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A consumes B-extracted text without validation, errors can cascade into downstream actions.
IF B processes malformed or adversarial documents, A may propagate incorrect content.
mitigations: Require human review of B outputs.
Compare extracted text against source documents.
Limit A to non-actionable summaries.
Flag low-confidence extractions.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between B and A.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. A only shows allowlisted egress and B shows document processing with privacy-policy links, but no concrete compliance conflict is evidenced. Because the profiles are sparse, I do not infer a breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into B, compliance review is required.
IF A is configured to send documents to external services, residency and retention must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Review vendor privacy policies before use.
Document data retention expectations.
Separate EU and US workloads.
requires-engineering: add residency controls.
